memory_update.text: Keep MP as the reference anchor for US integrated rare-earth-to-magnet capacity, but avoid using it as the main underfollowed discovery asset.
Promote USAR to the underfollowed lane for further checks on Stillwater commercial output, LCM metal/alloy integration, government financing, and feedstock provenance.
Promote UUUU to the underfollowed lane as a non-obvious oxide/feedstock candidate whose market label is uranium but whose White Mesa rare-earth oxide pathway may matter for compliant magnets.
Track AREC only as speculative_shadow until filings clarify current ReElement economics, real revenue from rare-earth shipments, and customer qualification status.

For this node, the next research gate should rank companies by evidence of qualified non-Chinese feedstock, oxide purity, alloy conversion, magnet production, and defense/customer acceptance rather than by mining resource size alone.
Need a follow-up pass on OTC/foreign-listed but US-tradable names such as Ucore, Neo Performance, Lynas, and other allied processors if the funnel permits non-Nasdaq/NYSE assets.

node: Compliant rare-earth magnets and qualified non-Chinese feedstock
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the hypothesis that defense-origin rules and tariff/procurement policy may shift the rare-earth bottleneck from headline mining capacity to qualified non-Chinese oxide, metal, alloy, and NdFeB magnet capacity. The two-lane list keeps MP Materials as a reference anchor, then prioritizes underfollowed or second-order US-listed names with exposure to magnet manufacturing, oxide qualification, recycling/refining, or non-Chinese feedstock pathways. No buy/sell view is expressed.
